messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] gff3 to bed conversion
messages.body_plain:
Dear Alejandro,

MethylKit and the UCSC uses the bed format with 12 columns. Detailed explanation is available from here <http://genome.ucsc.edu/FAQ/FAQformat.html#format1>. I will limit my explanation to the last two columns (11th and 12th).
11th column is about the sizes of the exons. The order of the numbers correspond to the order of the exons. Column no. 10 indicates the total number of exons and one will find an equivalent count of sizes in the 11th column.
12th column is about the distance from where each exon starts with relative to the 'chrstart' column(2nd column). Do not confuse it to the absolute genomic co-ordinate. It is relative to the 2nd column. (sometimes it is possible that 12th column is absent. I dont know why is it so. May be in cases like pseudo genes)
An eg for the last two co-ordinates is as follows:
chrom                                             :chr1
chromstart                                      : 52380633
chrromend                                      : 52502307
No. of exons                                   : 5 (column 10)
Size of each exon            :30,106,106,2108,275,(column 11)
Start of each exon (wrt chromstart): 0,73995,90797,95114,121399, (column 12)

I have two options you may consider for generating annotation objects for arabidopsis. I hope they may work in methylKit (not sure). Both these options utilise the bioconductor packages. So, I assume that you are familiar with them (Easy to work with). There may be some typos in the names of functions and packges listed below.

Option1
GenomicFeatures package from bioconductor offers a function makeTranscriptDbFromGFF. You may use this to generate the transcript database from the gff3 file you have. Once you have generated you may
generate separate objects for introns, exons, cds, genes, intergenic. Generated objects are 'GRanges' objects
Use functions from 'GenomicRanges' package to tweak the cds object to generate TSS ranges
combine all the needed 'GRanges' object into a 'GenomicRangesList' object. Note that the objects generated above can not be combined into a 'GRangesList'. To my understanding, every annotation functions that works for 'GRangesList' (used in methylKit) will also work for 'GenomicRangesList' objects
A worked out example for gencode human annotation is available on this blog post <http://chitka-kalyan.blogspot.fi/2014/02/creating-gencode-transcript-database-in.html>
Option2
Bioconductor has a ready to use transcript database for arabidopsis. You may check its relevance for your work. It is available from here <http://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/data/annotation/html/TxDb.Athaliana.BioMart.plantsmart19.html>. There are also other versions available for arabidopsis (search with keyword arabidopsis and look for packages that start with TxDb.Athaliana). Installing one of this package will reduce the task of building your own annotation files. You may then
use functions like cds,exons,genes,transcripts from 'GenomicFeatures' package to generate the 'GRanges' objects. You may follow the functions in the above blog post to generate whatever you need.
sometimes functions like cdsBy, exonsBy, transcriptsBy may also be useful
In case you want to limit your annotation to certain genes or features related to certain genes you may try 'select' function from 'AnnotationDbi' package.

Hope you will be able to work out.

Regards,
Kalyan

messages.body_plain:
Hi Saad,
How many CHG were captured in your dataset?
I am afraid that CHG might not fit the eDMR distance cutoff assumption. eDMR were developed based on the CpG methylation data and based on the bimodal distribution. But it looks like CHG methylation does not have this feature.
But if you can supply your own distance cutoff (N) to determine regions, then you can still use eDMR functions, specifying dist= N
I suggest you try a couple of N and see which results make more sense to you.
Cheers,
Sheng

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] order of sequences
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

In both cases you have mentioned you have got the identical results. However, you have to interpret them in the way you have considered your samples.

In methylkit, when one has multiple samples (say few of them are control and few are test). One has to mention (you did it) the control and test samples explicitly using treatment vector (I am expecting that you understand R). Control samples are indicated by '0' and test samples as '1'. What ever hypo or hyper methylation you observe in your results is the methylation status in test samples ( indicated by '1' in treatment vector) relative to control samples (indicated by '0' in treatment vector).

So, in the first case you have treated your 'control' samples as '1' which according to methylkit are 'test' samples (as indicated in treatment vector). In the second case you have treated 'test' samples as '1' and 'control' samples as '0' which is what you meant.

In both the above cases, you have got the same result. In simple english, it is like saying America is located west of europe but for America, europe is located eastwards. Both are correct but are relative!

Regards,
Kalyan
